newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares extend recovery as Dow opens firm.
newsitem.headline: German shares extend recovery as Dow opens firm.

text.p: German shares pushed further upwards in post-bourse electronic trade, as Wall Street opened firm, calming lingering nerves after heavy losses on Friday and raising hopes for a resumption of a pre-Christmas rally.

The gains came amid relief that last week's warnings against excessive market exuberance by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan did not have a disastrous impact on Wall Street and as Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said markets had overreacted to the comments.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day computerised dealings in the DAX index of 30 top German stocks, ended up 37.77 points, or 1.33 percent, at 2,870.30, well-above the floor trade close of 2,857.24 points.
The gains wiped out more than half of the DAX's four-percent slide before the weekend, which was triggered by Greenspan's remarks.
"People are starting to see that the first reaction was a bit too exaggerated," said one Frankfurt dealer.
"We are still in an uptrend," said another dealer. "The market has had the weekend to digest what happened last week and is in far calmer form."
Strength in German bonds and the dollar's return to trade over 1.55 marks were also helping to buoy stocks.
Gains were especially strong in stocks which had fallen hardest on Friday and exporters in the chemical and auto maker sectors, which were boosted by the renewed dollar strength.
Shares in chemicals group BASF AG were the biggest DAX gainer, ending IBIS dealings up 2.49 marks, or 4.25 percent at 61.14 marks.

Shares in carmaker Volkswagen AG, always volatile as the company's legal battle continues with U.S. giant General Motors Corp over alleged industrial espionage, jumped briefly after VW said its chairman was poised to express his regrets to GM over the issue.
GM had made a public apology one of its conditions for any settlement of the court case. VW shares hit a high of 608.75, but then settled up 5.85 marks at 602 marks.
